items.title: Apple, Exxon and Lowe’s Are Rewarding Shareholders Beyond Their Regular Dividends
items.summary: One of these three dividend payers yields just 0.30%, another has stopped buying back shares entirely, and the third just promised never to cut its payout. Each handles the cash differently, and the differences matter if you live on portfolio income.

items.title: Oil Markets Face Another Potential Threat to Household Fuel Costs
items.summary: A familiar global threat could complicate America's inflation outlook.

items.title: Investors 50 and Older Can Put $8,600 Into a Roth IRA in 2026 to Build Tax-Free Dividend Income
items.summary: Four household-name dividend stocks can quietly hand the IRS a four-figure bill every year, and one of them does most of the damage. Investors over 50 hold a special tool to fight back, but income limits can shut some couples out.

items.title: iShares S&P 500 Value ETF (IVE) Buys $31.4 Million More Apple on Nov. 24
items.summary: The $49.63 billion fund added to 429 positions and sold nothing, with Apple, Amazon and Exxon Mobil its largest purchases.

items.title: How Much You’d Need in Dividend Stocks to Generate $5,000 a Month in Passive Income
items.summary: The price tag on a $60,000 dividend paycheck swings by nearly $2 million depending on the yield you chase. Higher payouts shrink the bill, but one tier hides a trap that can gut your income when a cut arrives.

items.title: ExxonMobil (XOM) Stock Looks Cheap Against Future Cash Flow Estimates
items.summary: ExxonMobil Holdings has posted a powerful 5 year share gain, which makes the recent pullback a natural moment to ask whether the current price can still be explained by the cash flows the business is expected to generate. With the stock now trading at US$158.23 after a weaker month, the key issue is how that market value lines up against what a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) view of its future money generation suggests. ExxonMobil is up 212.9% over 5 years, which puts a lot of weight on the idea...

items.title: Energy Stocks Benefit From Supply Disruptions: Can Momentum Last?
items.summary: Rising crude prices and diesel shortages drive gains for Valero, Cheniere, Chevron and ExxonMobil, but recovering oil supplies could test their momentum.

items.title: Bad News for Exxon and Chevron: Goldman Sees Brent Falling “Roughly $10” Next Year on a Supply Glut
items.summary: Key TakeawaysGoldman Sachs expects Brent and WTI crude to fall about $10 over the next year on an oil surplus of about 2 million barrels a day. Consensus estimates for ExxonMobil, Chevron and ConocoPhillips still reflect this year’s wartime oil prices.
